text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 502/504 rate observed at API gateway (edge tier). error-rate spike started ~3387654300, current 5xx rate ~11% (baseline ~0.7%). Paging oncall.

sre-oncall: Ack. I'm on it. Assigning pager handoff to @kevin to coordinate edge/proxy side. Anyone actively rolling? :eyes:

kevin: Not aware of any canary. I see a cluster of 502s coming from edge-pop-us-east-1 -> upstream timeout to origin-pool-3. P95 latency on gateway jumped to 1.8s. Sharing logs.

maria: I see the same in traces. Increased retries and HTTP/1.1 connection resets. Clients: mobile-app and partner-ingest have most hits. PartnerA is showing increased error chatter in support.

ashley: On it, checking recent envoy config/route changes. No config commits in last 2 hours. No deploys tagged as prod-edge in last 3h.

platform-oncall: Looking at infra metrics: host CPU stable, but ephemeral connections on frontends doubled. Could be TCP exhaustion or DNS issues causing long connect latencies.

kevin: Good call. Can someone run a quick curl to gateway health endpoint and to upstream via proxy? Example: `curl -v -H "Host: api.redwood.ai" https://edge-us-east-1.redwood.ai/health` and `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:10.1.2.5 https://api.redwood.ai/` — please paste results.

maria: Health endpoint returns 200 from one edge node but intermittent 502 on others. `curl` to upstream via resolve shows `connect to 10.1.2.5 port 443 failed: Connection timed out` on some nodes, success on others.

prod-observability-bot: Metrics snapshot: gateway_5xx_rate: 11.2%, gateway_latency_p95: 1.82s, origin_connect_time_p95: 1.6s, dns_lookup_time_p95: 0.9s, active_conn_frontend: 4.2k (normally 2.0k). Spike began at 2026-03-15T10:45:00Z (ts 3387654300).

kevin: DNS lookup time p95 0.9s is suspicious. Are we seeing NXDOMAIN or heavy throttle from our internal DNS resolver? eng-router, can you check DNS forwarder health and cache hit rates?

eng-router: Checking local nodes — cache hit rate dropped to 30% from 98% around spike. Resolver logs show high retry/backoff to upstream DNS (10.11.11.5). Looks like resolver flapped.

ashley: If DNS is slow, clients waiting on connect could exhaust connection pools and lead to 502s from envoy. We should short-circuit by increasing resolver timeout or route to cached IPs while resolving root cause. Proposing temporary mitigation: switch edge routing to last-known-good upstream IPs for partner-heavy routes and enable aggressive HTTP/1.1 keepalive to reduce new DNS lookups.

sre-oncall: Agreed. Action items: 1) kevin/ashley to apply route override for partner-ingest prefix to pinned IPs. 2) platform-oncall to scale edge-proxy pool by 30% to relieve connection backlog. 3) eng-router to restart DNS forwarder on two nodes and failover to secondary resolver. 4) maria to monitor partnerA and mobile-app error rates. 5) If errors persist after 5m, roll traffic to fallback region (us-west-1).

kevin: Applying route override now for partner-ingest -> pin to 10.1.2.5,10.1.2.6. Command: `scripts/edge-route-override --route partner-ingest --ips 10.1.2.5,10.1.2.6 --ttl 300` — running.

ashley: Override applied on 4/6 edge nodes, rolling remainder. Confirmed config pushed via rollout service. :white_check_mark:

platform-oncall: Scaling edge-proxy ASG +30% (min->desired). New instances coming up.

eng-router: Restarted dns-forwarder on resolver-01 and resolver-03, promoted resolver-02 as primary. Cache hit rate climbing back to ~85%.

maria: PartnerA error rate down from 18% -> 4.5% since override + DNS fix. Mobile-app errors also trending down. Latency p95 dropped to 0.9s.

prod-observability-bot: Post-mitigation snapshot: gateway_5xx_rate: 3.8%, gateway_latency_p95: 0.95s, origin_connect_time_p95: 0.7s, dns_lookup_time_p95: 0.12s.

sre-oncall: Nice work. We're in mitigation. Are we confident this is resolver instability and not an upstream origin flake?

eng-router: Logs show origin TCP resets were correlated with DNS delays causing repeated connection attempts and SYN retries. No evidence of origin-side resource exhaustion. We'll keep investigating origin logs but current evidence points to resolver/hairy cache.

kevin: Starting a full sweep of edge-proxy envoy stats for anomalies and socket states (`netstat -anp | grep TIME_WAIT`). Will share if anything odd.

ashley: Also flagging this for a follow-up RCA: DNS forwarder capacity, fallback resolver policies, and route override automation. Need to ensure we have graceful fallback to pinned IPs when resolver slip occurs.

sre-oncall: Customer impact summary for postmortem: Incident window 3387654300 -> 3387654660 (about 6 minutes major spike, then degradation). Peak affected traffic window ~3m. Maximum error rate peaked ~11-19% across regions. Major customers impacted: PartnerA (high), mobile-web (medium). No PII or data loss reported. Severity: sev2 (customer-facing outage with partial degradation).

platform-oncall: Handoff to infra for deeper DNS analysis and to eng-router for residual remediation. I'll create an incident ticket and move this to #postmortems with links to graphs and logs.

prod-observability-bot: Created incident-18392 in ops tracker: https://redwood.ops/incidents/18392 (includes graphs, traces, and alert timeline).

sre-oncall: OK handing off primary ownership to eng-router and infra. If anything flares back, page SRE again. Closing live triage. Thanks everyone. :bow:

kevin: Leaving a short runbook snippet here for next time:
```
1) Check prod observability DNS latency and cache hit rate
2) If DNS lookup_time_p95 > 200ms -> failover DNS and consider pinned IPs
3) Scale edge-proxy pool +30% if active_conn_frontend > baseline*2
4) Apply route override for impacted prefixes (TTL 300) while resolving
```

maria: Adding a user-impact blurb for comms: "We observed a short-lived spike in 5xx errors affecting API gateway traffic between 10:45–10:52 UTC; most requests recovered after edge routing and DNS failover. Our teams are investigating root cause and will publish an RCA." Please review and approve before we post to status.

sre-oncall: Approved. Moving thread to #postmortems. Last note: kudos to everyone for quick mitigation. :tada:
